hook: Power for AI, SAP job cuts, school pushback and robot bets
open: Tonight, JERA courts Anthropic and Meta, SAP plans deep job cuts, and Los Angeles schools push back on Google.
summary: Japan's JERA is in talks with Anthropic and Meta on data centers near Tokyo power plants, and SAP is reportedly readying 10,000-plus job cuts.
Los Angeles schools quietly turned off AI search summaries, and the UK competition watchdog set out control rules as Meta's Muse agent launched.
Morgan Stanley expects humanoid robot investment in China to speed up, with selective commercial use in 2027.

stories.headline: Japan's JERA enters talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres
stories.summary: Japan's largest power generator, JERA, is in talks with Anthropic and Meta to build data centres near power plants around Tokyo. The discussions form part of JERA's broader infrastructure push, which includes a planned $15 billion hyperscale data centre in Chiba.
stories.why_it_matters: The discussions illustrate how major energy suppliers are coordinating directly with artificial intelligence developers to secure dedicated power sources for heavy computing demands.

stories.headline: SAP prepares plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions for AI shift
stories.summary: SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions, or 9% of its global staff. The restructuring aims to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era.
stories.why_it_matters: The restructuring highlights how major enterprise software providers are shifting capital and human resources away from traditional operations to prioritize artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Los Angeles school district blocks AI search features on student devices
stories.summary: Los Angeles Unified School District has temporarily disabled AI-generated search summaries on school-issued devices amid growing friction between school districts and Google over bundled artificial intelligence tools. The half-million-student district made the change without a formal public announcement following concerns from parent and activist groups.
stories.why_it_matters: While school districts previously announced temporary moratoriums on generative AI use, this action represents a technical workaround implemented by a major district against a dominant technology provider that has stated it will not separate search products from education AI tools.

stories.headline: UK regulator warns AI agents must provide user control as Meta Muse launches
stories.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority warned that businesses offering personal AI agents must give consumers control over data access and agent autonomy. The guidance follows Meta's launch of its personal AI agent, Muse, in the UK.
stories.why_it_matters: UK regulators are actively setting compliance boundaries for autonomous AI tools as Big Tech products enter the market.

stories.headline: China humanoid robot investment to rise, selective use by 2027
stories.summary: Investment in humanoid robots in China is projected to accelerate, with selective commercial use anticipated in 2027 according to a Morgan Stanley report. The report highlights that spending on data collection, robot training, and early customer deployments is likely to increase.
stories.why_it_matters: Component suppliers could benefit from rising hardware orders even before humanoid robots see widespread commercial adoption.
